html:
The Tuscarora, or Skarù꞉ręʔ ("hemp gatherers"), are an Iroquoian people who in 1492 lived on the coastal plain of what is now North Carolina, along the Roanoke, Tar and Neuse rivers. They farmed maize and lived in towns, the largest Iroquoian people of the south.

English settlers moving into their land took captives as slaves and cheated them in trade. In 1711 the Tuscarora struck back, starting the Tuscarora War. Colonial troops from both Carolinas, with Catawba and Yamasee allies, burned their fort of Neoheroka in 1713, killing or enslaving hundreds. Most survivors went north and in 1722 were adopted into the Haudenosaunee Confederacy as its sixth nation. Their descendants live near Niagara Falls in New York and on the Six Nations reserve in Ontario. Their old neighbours on the coast included the Secotan and the Chowanoke. The map also has a separate Tuscarora territory.
